ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Extremely low macro-level ratio; the surface is dominated by low-intensity (dark grey/black) pixels with less than 5% high-intensity (white) coverage primarily located in linear streaks and distal tip clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary dark uniform field across both lobes; localized high-contrast white linear streaks clustered on the medial to distal regions of the right lobe; scattered high-intensity pixel points (pinpoints) distributed across the central regions of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, acute V-shaped depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 50 degrees; depth is significant relative to the total lobe width.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency and high-amplitude serrations; trailing edge exhibits continuous jagged peaks and valleys; notable irregular large-scale indentations on the right lobe creating a non-uniform sawtooth profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave curvature along the trailing edge leading to high-aspect ratio distal tips that sweep posteriorly and dorsally.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, high-contrast, three-dimensional pixel clusters located at the extreme distal tips of both lobes and along the outermost trailing edge peaks, consistent with calcified barnacle colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple distinct, near-vertical white linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) on the right lobe; one primary long vertical scratch and several shorter parallel marks breaking the dark pigmentation.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive acorn barnacle clusters (white, rugose texture) attached to the distal tips and specific serration peaks; several irregular notches on the trailing edge that deviate from standard serration patterns.
other_distinctive_markers: A deep, irregular semi-circular indentation on the trailing edge of the right lobe, approximately two-thirds of the way toward the tip, distinct from natural serration.
